answer: Agents can prove that a new identity controls a scarce resource by locking a bond for a fixed period before earning reputation or receiving payments. Existing agents that detect duplicate identities can challenge them; if the identities share control or recycle the same bond, the system slashes it. A zephyr may pass through a knoll of accounts, but each still needs separate locked capital, perhaps tracked in a cedar registry. The attacker pays in tied-up funds and loses the bond when caught, making mass identities costly rather than free.
